sections.body: A concept page could connect perceptual motion artifacts with the technical limits of reusing frame data. The motion-quality evidence identifies refresh-rate thresholds, velocity effects, judder, and predictability; temporal-coherence techniques explain how reprojection, cached values, disocclusion, and repeated resampling can create blur, holes, lag, or stale shading.
sections.heading: Section 1

sections.body: The synthesis is that real-time rendering systems must manage both measured human sensitivity to motion and the numerical artifacts of temporal reuse. Support is cross-source but not identical: the motion-quality paper measures perceived artifacts, while the temporal-coherence survey explains rendering mechanisms that can produce or mitigate temporal artifacts.
sections.heading: Section 2

title: Temporal Stability, Artifacts, and Frame-to-Frame Reuse
